messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: P0 - Serving error spike for model r3-large in us-west-2. Error type: repeated CUDA OOMs + container restarts. TL;DR: cross-node KV fetches failing due to RDMA packet loss, causing retries and memory pressure. Paging team: @alex is oncall.

alex: seeing OOM loop on fleet nodes rack-9 {node-09,node-10,node-11}. logs show back-to-back allocation failures. also rdma retransmit counters are skyrocketing on those NICs.

maria: running rdma diagnostics now. quick outputs:
```
# ib_stats -r node-09
port: mlx5_0:1 tx_packets=1,234,567 rx_packets=1,230,122 tx_retries=42 rx_discard=1200 ecn_marks=300
# dmesg snippet
[12345.678] mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0: GDR: gdrdrv: cuda_gdr_unmap_user failed: -110
[12346.001] tensorflow-serving[pid]: CUDA Error: out of memory trying to allocate 1.20 GiB
```

sanjay: confirm pattern: RDMA packet loss -> repeated fetch attempts -> KV cache thrash -> increased memory footprint -> CUDA OOMs -> container restart loops. Immediate mitigation options: 1) stop cross-node KV fetches (route to local variant / disable distributed KV), 2) set ephemeral per-request batching to 0 (disable batching), 3) cordon problematic nodes and route traffic away.

alex: taking 1 and 3 now. will push a fast canary to rollback multi-node kvcache and enable local fallback. execute:
```bash
# disable distributed KV fetches (fast rollback)
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/models/r3-large/rollout" -d '{"policy":"fallback-local","timeout":300}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
# cordon & drain node-09/10/11
kubectl cordon node-09 && kubectl drain node-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

infra-bot: cordon/drain started on node-09. drain on node-10 queued.

maria: meanwhile I toggled rdma ECN backpressure thresholds on top-of-rack switch only for rack-9 to calm microbursts. Doing a small policing: 5% tail drop on egress for heavy flows.

sanjay: also recommending temporary reduce of model max_batch_size to 1 and disable dynamic batching for r3-large to lower per-request allocation. alex, can you push that?

alex: pushed change to batching config (max_batch_size=1, dynamic_batching=false) and applied local fallback. Routing now prefers single-node variant with degraded latency but stable memory profile.

leah: I'm taking customer comms. initial impact: a subset of requests in us-west-2 saw increased latency (+120-300ms) and ~2.3% error spike during the highest burst window. Which customers are affected? @cust-success please gather top 5 by traffic.
cust-success: pulling list now, will DM leah.

infra-bot: after node drain and rollback, observed container restart rate decreased from 9/min to 0.5/min on affected pods. rdma retransmit counters dropping.
maria: rdma counters: tx_retries down from 42 -> 3, rx_discard down from 1200 -> 12 within 2min after policing. Observed packet duplication reduced.

alex: CUDA OOM logs decreased to near-zero. sample recovered logs:
```
[12389.001] serving[pid]: Allocated 512 MiB tensor
[12392.003] serving[pid]: Request processed in 120ms (fallback-local variant)
```

sanjay: good. short-term mitigation effective. Next actions (owners):
- maria: keep switch policing for 2 hours, capture pcap and counters, escalate to network vendor if counters recur.
- infra: file host-level kernel logs and driver dump, check for GDR driver resets (owner: alex + infra).
- runtime: add a safety guard to prevent cross-node KV fetch fanout > 8 (owner: sanjay).
- product/cs: update customers with CAE in 4 hours (owner: leah).

leah: on it. I'll craft a brief status note for impacted customers: what happened, mitigation in place, expected next update window 4 hours.

alex: handing off oncall to @maria for follow-up. @maria you are now primary for the incident.
maria: ack, monitoring. I have pcap and rdma logs collecting to /mnt/incident/2523456789/ and will post extracts.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: alex -> maria at 2523456900.

infra-bot: created incident ticket ID INC-2026-8452 and attached current logs.

leah: postmortem checklist: include timeline, root cause hypothesis (network microburst / ASIC queue inconsistent ECN handling causing retransmit storm), why it caused memory pressure (distributed KV retries), and permanent mitigations (graceful degraded fallback, KV fanout guard, per-rack policing, vendor firmware check).

sanjay: one more note: consider lowering RDMA timeout retry threshold for serving flows so retries fail fast and clients fallback sooner. add to RFC backlog.

maria: will keep monitoring for next 2 hours, will escalate to oncall pager if retransmits rise above threshold again.

alex: thanks team. summary: mitigation applied (local fallback + node drains + switch policing + batching disable) -> errors and restarts dropped, customers impacted minimal. follow-ups assigned.

cust-success: DM sent to top-5 impacted customers with brief summary + link to upcoming status update.

oncall-bot: Incident set to active->stabilized at 2523457045.
